You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Applied Materials Q3 Earnings Preview: Can AI-Driven Equipment Demand Support Strong Growth and Guidance Upside?

TEXT:
1. Investment Highlights Overview
Applied Materials ( AMAT .US) will report fiscal third-quarter 2026 results after the U.S. market close on August 13, 2026. Wall Street consensus expects revenue of approximately $9.0 billion (+23.3% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of about $3.39 (+36.7% YoY). The company’s prior guidance midpoint stands at revenue of $8.95 billion (±$500 million) and non-GAAP EPS of $3.36 (±$0.20), largely in line with market expectations. The stock has gained over 100% year-to-date but remains roughly 25% below its late-June all- time high. Investors are closely watching the sustainability of AI-related capital spending, contributions from advanced packaging and HBM, and whether management can again raise its full-year semiconductor equipment growth outlook.
2. Four Key Focus Areas
Focus 1: Strength of AI-Driven Leading-Edge and HBM Demand
Leading-edge Foundry/Logic, DRAM (especially HBM), and advanced packaging are viewed by management as the primary drivers of 2026 wafer fab equipment (WFE) growth, expected to account for more than 80% of the year’s incremental WFE spending. The market will scrutinize actual shipments and order momentum in these three areas to confirm whether expanding AI compute demand continues to translate into equipment purchases.
Focus 2: Semiconductor Systems Performance and Delivery on >30% Full-Year Growth Guidance
Management previously raised its calendar-year 2026 semiconductor equipment growth outlook to more than 30% , with advanced packaging expected to grow over 50% . Q3 Semiconductor Systems guidance is approximately $6.9 billion , the core growth engine this quarter. Attention will center on whether this segment beats expectations and on management’s comments regarding continued strong growth into 2027.
Focus 3: Gross Margin and Profitability Expansion Potential
Non-GAAP gross margin reached 50% in Q2 (a 25-year high), with Q3 guidance at roughly 50.1% . Whether the high-value product mix and scale benefits can further lift gross and operating margins will be key to assessing earnings quality. The Applied Global Services (AGS) long-term growth rate has been raised to the mid-teens; its contribution stability also warrants monitoring.
Focus 4: Q4 Guidance and Room for Full-Year Outlook Upside
Investors are placing greater emphasis on the next-quarter (Q4) guidance level. Some institutions expect a notably stronger outlook than consensus and further confirmation of calendar-year equipment growth target s. An upward revision to full-year guidance or stronger visibility commentary could serve as a sentiment catalyst.
3. Risks and Opportunities Coexist
Upside Catalysts:
Revenue and EPS meaningfully above consensus, paired with robust Q4 guidance (some institutions look for levels approaching or exceeding $10 billion).
Advanced packaging and HBM-related revenue contributions exceeding expectations, validating the breadth of AI demand.
Management reaffirming or raising the >30% full-year semiconductor equipment growth target and signaling optimism for 2027.
Downside Risks:
Results merely meeting the guidance midpoint without an upward full-year revision, compounded by high valuation and profit-taking after the recent pullback.
Further signs of softening in China exposure or mature-node demand.
Customer capital-spending cadence falling short of expectations, raising questions about the durability of the AI equipment cycle.
4. Trading Strategy Suggestions
Current price around 550-553 . Key supports at 520-525 and 505-515 ; resistances at 555-565 and 580-600 .
Bullish logic: If earnings beat expectations and the stock holds firmly above 555 , consider a light long entry on a pullback to that level, with a stop-loss below 520 and targets at 580-600 . Bearish risk: If guidance is muted and the price breaks below 520-525 , watch for short-term selling pressure.
Prioritize waiting for the post-close earnings reaction before acting, and strictly control position size with stop-losses.
Disclaimer: For reference only, not investment advice.
Key Data Points:
Total revenue and year-over-year growth
Semiconductor Systems revenue and sub-segment performance (Foundry/Logic, DRAM, packaging)
Non-GAAP gross margin and operating margin
Q4 revenue/EPS guidance and full-year semiconductor equipment growth commentary
Operational Suggestions: If both results and guidance exceed expectations, consider opportunities on any post-earnings pullback. If results are in-line or the outlook is soft, watch for short-term volatility risk and avoid chasing. Position sizing and stop-loss levels should be adjusted flexibly according to individual risk tolerance.
